headline: Every major sits above its 200-day line while the day, week, and month all point different directions
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's uniform in a way that doesn't happen often: BTC, ETH, SOL, BNB and XRP are all above their 200-day moving averages, with ETH and SOL sporting golden crosses. DOGE and ADA are the odd ones out, sitting below trend. Seven majors, five in an uptrend structurally, that's a market where the dominant current still runs up, even if today's tape is red almost everywhere (total market cap down 2.98% on the day).

But look at momentum and you find the first crack: every single asset in this set shows MACD below signal, even as RSI readings sit in the high 50s to mid 60s, nowhere near oversold, nowhere near euphoric either. That's a market cooling off inside an uptrend, not breaking one. BTC is a clean example: up 16.7% on the month, down 2.4% on the week, down just 0.3% on the day. Three windows, three different stories, which is exactly why you name the window every time you talk about direction here. XRP, DOGE and ADA show the sharpest version of this: all up double digits on the month, all down roughly 9-10% on the week. The trend is intact, the last seven days have not been kind to it.

Positioning adds a wrinkle worth sitting with. Funding is unremarkable across the board (BTC at 6.9% annualized, ETH at 11%, SOL barely positive at 0.5%), so nobody is paying a steep premium to stay long. Yet long/short account ratios lean heavily long everywhere: XRP at 2.43, DOGE at a striking 4.23, SOL at 1.92. Cheap funding with a crowded long ledger is an odd combination, it says retail accounts are stacked long without yet paying up for it. The liquidation windows lean toward longs getting hurt more than shorts in ETH (664,860 vs 28,068 over 2 hours) and XRP (754,471 vs 199,614 over 14 hours), while BTC shorts have taken the bigger hit (664,717 vs 292,185 over 9 hours). Mixed signal, no dominant squeeze in either direction.

The flow picture disagrees with itself in a way the data insists you say plainly. On the ETF side, the latest print (02 Sep 2026) shows BTC ETFs with a net outflow of $14.3M and ETH ETFs with a net outflow of $49.7M for the day. Zoom out to the last five sessions and both flip positive: BTC net inflow of $6.3M, ETH net inflow of $374.4M. Same-direction-day counts of 2 and 1 respectively confirm these are not settled trends, just a single day's number sitting against a five-day sum pointing the other way. Whale activity tells a cleaner story over 48 hours: $362.2M net moved off exchanges, led by BTC, with the biggest single moves being BTC leaving Coinbase ($172.5M) and Kraken ($156.1M). The weekly whale series shows this is a recent turn, not an old habit: the three prior weeks (ending Aug 13, Aug 20, Aug 27) all show large net flows onto exchanges, the week ending Sep 03 is the first to flip off-exchange, and only by $344M. Stablecoin float is up just 1.16% over 30 days, sitting at $309B, dry powder growing slowly, not surging.

Sentiment reads Greed at 65, near the top of its own 30-day range of 25 to 74, while the tape underneath is broadly red on the day and mixed on the week. That gap between a greedy crowd and a market that's down 2.98% in market cap today is the kind of disagreement worth just noticing rather than explaining away. What to watch from here: whether the five-session ETF flow (currently positive for both BTC and ETH) starts printing positive daily numbers too, whether the weekly whale flow builds on this week's modest off-exchange net or reverts to the onto-exchange pattern seen in the three weeks prior, and whether MACD crosses back above signal on any major, which would say the pause in momentum is over rather than ongoing.
